title: Taste and See That the Lord Is Good
summary: David wrote this psalm hiding in a cave. Whatever we are facing, we can run to the Savior who was brokenhearted for us and taste his goodness.
exhortation: Notice that David doesn't say, "Trust me, the Lord is good," or "Read that the Lord is good." He says, "Taste and see."

David didn't write this psalm from his king's bed in his palace. He wrote it in a cave, hiding from Saul and his army, who were trying to hunt him down and kill him. The title of the psalm says it was written when he went before Abimelech and pretended to be insane just to get out of that situation. And there he is in a cave, writing this psalm.

Later in the psalm he says that the Lord is near to the brokenhearted and saves the crushed in spirit. So if this is you this morning, if you're feeling crushed or brokenhearted, like you're hiding out in a cave, David is right there with you. He understands. And more than that, our Savior understands. Our Savior was crushed. Our Savior was brokenhearted. Most of us know that when the spear pierced his side, water and blood flowed out, and many believe that is a sign of a literally broken heart.

And that same Savior, who rose and conquered the grave, says to us, "Come to me, all who are weary and heavy laden, and I will give you rest." So we have great reason this morning, no matter what situation we find ourselves in, to lift our eyes to Jesus, to run to him in times of trouble, and to bring him our broken hearts and our distress. That's our goal this morning: to lift our eyes to Jesus and find that in him is all goodness and all that we need.
prayer: Lord, I pray that we would not only know that you are good, think that you are good, or read that you are good, but that we would taste and see that you are good. That we would know it with a real knowledge that makes our faith strong as rock, because once we've tasted, it transforms us.

I pray for every person opening their Bible this morning and reading your word: may they taste and see that you are good. For everyone lifting up a prayer to you: may they taste and see that you are good. For everyone struggling through a trial: may they taste and see that you are good. And then may they declare with their mouths that you are good, and speak of your goodness just as David did. Thank you, Jesus, for your broken body, for the water and the blood that flowed for us, that we might taste and see that you are good. Amen.
